core_obligations: Observe that a purely inseparable base change induces a homeomorphism on underlying topological spaces, so there is a unique point above x and the local ring there is the tensor product of the local ring at x with the field (proof lines 479-484).
Apply the pointwise criterion for geometric reducedness to convert the scheme statement into a statement about local rings (proof lines 485-486).

Apply the algebra criterion testing geometric reducedness over finite purely inseparable extensions, and note that the single extension and the perfect closure cases are covered by the same equivalence (proof lines 486-487).
proof_roadmap: Purely inseparable base change as a homeomorphism (proof lines 479-484).
Algebraic criterion for purely inseparable extensions (proof lines 486-487).
difficulty_reason: In characteristic p, for a scheme X over k and a point x, the lemma gives four equivalent conditions: geometric reducedness at x, reducedness of the local rings at the unique lifted points for all finite purely inseparable extensions, reducedness for the single extension k^{1/p}, and reducedness after the perfect closure (statement lines 462-476). The proof first notes that a purely inseparable base change induces a homeomorphism on the underlying spaces, which both explains the uniqueness of the lifted point and identifies the local ring upstairs with the tensor product of the local ring at x with the field; the equivalence then follows from the pointwise criterion for geometric reducedness together with the algebra criterion for purely inseparable extensions (proof lines 478-487). The claim is H2: one topological observation about purely inseparable base changes plus two cited criteria, with the identification of the local ring as the bridge.
